reason: Research was limited: three web searches and one fetch, none of which found an Oct 9 closing wrap, so the marks come from the packet and the macro picture from Oct 5-6 reports. On Oct 5 the 10y was at 5.34% and the 30y at 5.70%, the highest since 2002, with roughly a 25% chance priced for an October Fed hike and a full 25bp hike by December. Brent was around $98-102 on Middle East risk, gold near $4,180, and equities near records on poor breadth. That is the oil-driven stagflation regime this book was rebuilt for on 10-05, so the thesis has not changed in four sessions. The managed-care recovery trade, 30% in UNH plus CI, faces its catalyst right after entry: Zacks (a single secondary source, unconfirmed by the company) dates UNH's Q3 report to Oct 13. The question is whether Q2's 86.7% MCR, helped by $860M of favorable reserve development, holds against the 88.1% full-year guide. I sized UNH at 16% with a 12% stop specifically to own that print, and cutting it the day before would abandon the trade at its moment of truth. All seven equity legs are in profit (+0.2% to +7.2%) and none is near its stop or take-profit. ETH at -8.3% is a 3% sleeve with a 20% stop, so its risk is already capped. A full replacement would pay real basis points to arrive at the same book. Hold and let the standing stops do the work.
